appendix_title: GROUPING OF PĀÑCARĀTRA TEXTS According to Siddhānta-ratnākara
content:
Appendix V
GROUPING OF
PĀÑCARĀTRA TEXTS
According to Siddhānta-ratnākara

1. DIVYA GROUP (11):
Sāttvata, Pauskara, Jayākhya, Aniruddha, Samkarşana, Hayagriva, Varāha, Pradyumna, Vāmana, Nārāyana, and Vāsudeva Samhitās.

2. MUNI-BHĀȘITA:
(a) Sāttvika (26):
Īsvara, Bhāradvāja, Pāramesvara, Sumantu, Vaihāyasa, Citra-sikhandi, Jayottara, Vasistha, Parāsara, Vişnu, Hiranya-garbha, Visvāmitra, Sāndilya, Padma, Mahendra, Visvaksena, Bhārgava, Vihagendra, Ananta, Parama-puruşa, Ahirbudhnya, Khaga-prasna, Nāradīya, Durvāsa, Sanaka and Agastya Samhitās.

(b) Rājasa (30)
Santkumāra, Padmodbhava, Satya, Tejodravina, Māyā-vaib-hava, Atreya, Kātyāyana, Saunakiya, Kāsyapa, Mārkandeya, Kāpiñjalam, Sāra-samuccaya, Visva, Nala-Kūbara, Trailokya-mohana, Yoga-hrdaya, Samvarta, Brahma-siddhānta, Vāgīsa, Saumya, Sāraka, Ānanda, Mūla, Upendra, Puști, Marīca, Gār-gya, Aupagāyana, Brhaspati and Nārasimha Samhitās.

Appendix V ♦ 179

(c) Tāmasa (26)
Panca-prasna, Suka-prasna, Tattva-sāgara, Gautama, Sātātapa, Yājñavalkya, Paulastya, Dattātreya, Kātyāyana, Kārşna, Bodhāyana, Kāpila, Jaimini, Kaumāra, Vāmadeva, Vāyaviya, Pārāvata, Vārna, Umā-mahesvara, Āgneya, Sārva, Jāmadagnya, Dhanada, Satya, Srīkara and Jābāla Samhitās
summary: This appendix, titled "GROUPING OF PĀÑCARĀTRA TEXTS," presents a classification system for Pāñcarātra literature according to the authority of the Siddhānta-ratnākara. The texts are divided into two main categories: the Divya (divine) group, consisting of 11 texts, and the Muni-Bhāṣita (spoken by sages) group. The Muni-Bhāṣita group is further subdivided into three classes based on the gunas: Sāttvika (26 texts), Rājasa (30 texts), and Tāmasa (26 texts). In total, the appendix lists 93 distinct Samhitās or texts.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to provide a structured and traditional categorization of the vast corpus of Pāñcarātra texts. By organizing them into groups based on their perceived origin (divine vs. sage) and nature (sāttvika, rājasa, tāmasa), it offers a framework for scholars and practitioners to understand the relationships and characteristics of these important religious scriptures.
key_information: The classification is based on the Siddhānta-ratnākara.
Pāñcarātra texts are divided into two primary groups: Divya and Muni-Bhāṣita.
The Muni-Bhāṣita group is subdivided into Sāttvika (26 texts), Rājasa (30 texts), and Tāmasa (26 texts).
A total of 93 texts are listed across all categories.
